gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: You ___ park here — the police tow cars away every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses a rule you must not break: mustn't park.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: The invoices ___ last week, so the delay is entirely our fault.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have + participle' criticises a past omission; passive adds 'been sent'.
